newsitem.title: FRANCE: EVA Air to use 747 combis permanently Paris-Taipei.
newsitem.headline: EVA Air to use 747 combis permanently Paris-Taipei.

text.p: Eva Air plans to deploy Boeing 747 combi aircraft on a permanent basis on its Paris-Taipei route later this year, a Paris-based cargo official for the Taiwanese airline told Reuters.
The combis were re-introduced at the end of March 1997, having replaced 747 passenger aircraft on a three-times-weekly service, which is operated via Vienna and Bangkok, the official said.
The combis themselves had been replaced by the passenger planes in June 1996.
"The combis will continue to ply the Paris-Taipei route until June 19 when passenger aircraft will replace them once again and operate during the the peak tourist season," the official said.
The combis will return to the route on September 19, he added.
Eva Air's Paris cargo office has an allocation of around 20 tonnes per flight on to the combis compared to only seven to eight tonnes on 747 passenger aircraft.

"There is a good level of demand at present on the route for a wide range of general cargo and the combis' extra capacity is well appreciated. We look to having them on a permanent basis from the autumn," he said."
The Paris office will also have a 10-tonne per flight allocation on Eva Air's new twice-weekly MD-11 freighter service from Brussels to Taipei, scheduled for launch on May 10, the official added.
